---
name: Legal typography authorization
description: Scope of the authorized formatting fallback and immutable legal evidence boundary
---

Missing original document fonts are authorized grounds for formatting the entire new working document in a consistent licensed serif family, not grounds for rewriting clauses or repairing historical evidence.

**Why:** The user explicitly replaced the former exact-font-only policy with Liberation Serif at 12 points. This permission applies to new working documents only, while uploaded originals, historical generated files, investor-signed documents and signing evidence remain immutable.

**How to apply:** Keep legal wording and supplied signature images unchanged. Pagination changes are permitted, but signature placement must still validate against the final PDF; never loosen that check merely to make a reformatted template activate. Tests of the original-layout branch need controlled font readiness rather than the former test-environment bypass.

Authoring highlights are intentionally absent from newly issued documents and
illustrative previews, but historical PDFs may still show them. That difference
is not permission to regenerate or replace historical evidence.

**Why:** On 2026-10-02 the user explicitly authorized output-only highlight
removal and excluded previously issued or signed artifacts from the change.

**How to apply:** Keep source downloads highlighted and byte-identical. If a
missing historical PDF cannot be recreated with its recorded digest, stop for
investigation rather than saving a visually corrected replacement.

Explicit administrator authoring is separate from automatic typography changes:
admins may change template wording within the app, saving a new inactive version.
This does not authorize automatic clause changes during conversion or replacement
of previously issued investor documents.

**Why:** The user requested in-app editing of both the deed and transfer agreement
and reiterated that downloading Word is not a substitute for an admin editor.
The existing immutable-evidence boundaries remain in force.

**How to apply:** Preserve the original Word structures and signature assets when
authoring wording; do not reconstruct legal forms from generic HTML. Keep automatic
investor fields protected. Preview and activation remain explicit separate steps;
existing investor pairs retain their pinned versions.

In-app editing must be discoverable in the main property legal workspace, not
offered only as a download or a control behind secondary navigation.

**Why:** The user reiterated that there was no editor visible in the app even
when the published code contained a template-editing flow. Code presence and
navigation instructions alone did not satisfy the requested admin experience.

**How to apply:** Verify direct access to both document editors from the default
property workspace, including mobile and clear load/missing-source states. Report
workspace availability and published availability separately.
